title: SOLAR RADIATION PREDICTION USING MACHINE LEARNING
abstract: Worldwide solar radiation is a basic parameter for the plan andoperation frameworks. Long-standing records of worldwide solar radiation data are not accessible in many places because of the cost and maintenance of the measuring instruments. Sun based radiation expecta- tion contains a incredible significance in power generation from sun based energy and makes a difference to measure photovoltaic control frameworks. With this context, we have utilized solar radiation dataset extracted from UCI Machine Learning. The forecasting of solar radiation are attained in four ways. Firstly, the data set is analyzed and preprocessed with Feature Scaling and missing values. Secondly, the correlation of the features is done and the relation of each features are visualized.

title: Derived data and statistical analysis code for diagnosing multimodal model failures on K12 mathematics multiple choice questions with images
abstract: This record provides de-identified derived data and reconstructed statistical analysis code accompanying the manuscript "Diagnosing multimodal model failures on K12 mathematics multiple choice questions with images". The main dataset contains 1,400 model-item outcome records from 200 image-based mathematics multiple-choice questions evaluated using seven publicly deployed AI assistant services across Zhongkao, AMC, SAT, and HK-DSE. It records extracted final-answer correctness and four diagnostic failure-category indicators: Visual Perception Failure (VPF), Spatial Reasoning Deficiency (SRD), Subject Knowledge Deficiency (SKD), and Logical/Symbolic Failure (LSF). The archive also contains 140 supplementary selective structured-prompt records, retained annotation-agreement contingency counts, response-status summaries, analysis scripts, statistical results, and automated tests. The Python code reproduces Cochran's Q, 21 exact pairwise McNemar comparisons with Holm adjustment, four item-clustered logistic GEE analyses with Holm correction across 24 non-intercept service contrasts, and descriptive error-label analyses. The scripts were reconstructed from retained research records; they do not re-run the model evaluations. Original examination images, complete question texts, and full model-response transcripts are not included. The selective structured-prompt results are descriptive and should not be interpreted as a fully retested causal effect.

title: Certified Accounting for Adaptive Shuffled Gaussian Training
abstract: This preprint develops a certified privacy accountant for multi-epoch shuffled training with Gaussian noise, heterogeneous items, and queries that adapt to earlier releases. A null-clone reduction bounds likelihood sums by candidate count and produces a finite rational dominating pair that composes across epochs. For 1,000 batches per epoch, five epochs, noise multiplier 1, and delta = 10^-8, the paper brackets the worst-case epsilon of the full adaptive transcript in (6.423, 7.97], while matched Poisson sampling is certified at 0.507. It also gives an adaptive counterexample to the proposed dominating pair of Chua et al. The dominating-pair construction, counterexample, and supporting certificate lemmas are formalized in Lean 4; the paper identifies the reduction and other steps that remain in the written proofs.

title: Product Monte Carlo: Expectation Under a Product of Densities
abstract: Aggregating independently computed sub-sample inferences is a well-known challenge in large-scale Bayesian computation, federated learning, and opinion pooling. The core problem is to approximate a distribution whose density is proportional to a product of individual densities. We propose Product Monte Carlo (PMC), an algorithm for computing arbitrary expectations under a product of densities using only Monte Carlo draws from individual densities. We turn the intractable product expectation into a regression problem by expressing it through a family of computable conditional expectations. Besides the point estimate, our fully Bayesian regression formulation provides coherent uncertainty quantification and principled diagnostics. We establish theoretical guarantees on consistency and characterize convergence rates for the PMC estimator. Across simulated and real-data experiments varying the number, dimensionality, and heterogeneity of the component distributions, PMC achieves higher estimation accuracy, better-calibrated uncertainty coverage, and improved scalability at a lower computational cost than existing methods. In addition, PMC requires no density evaluation, making it applicable to simulation-based inference, as we demonstrate in an application with protein images.

title: EWOCS-XI: Anisotropic expansion and shear in the cluster Westerlund 1. A 2D kinematic analysis with Gaia DR3
abstract: Westerlund 1 (Wd1) is one of the Milky Way's most massive young clusters, in which heavy extinction and field contamination have historically hampered its kinematic characterization. We aim to assess Wd1's internal kinematics, dynamical state, and formation scenario. Using a robust 5D clustering approach, we identified 559 bona fide members. We modeled their proper motions via a 2D first-order Taylor expansion to derive the velocity gradient tensor, mapping expansion, rotation, and shear. Restricting the kinematic analysis to 524 stars with proper motion uncertainties <0.5~mas,yr^{-1}, we find at least 103 gravitationally unbound members, including 14 walkaway stars. The 2D analysis reveals a statistically significant divergence (>4σ) highlighting preferred expansion along the Galactic latitude (position angle 164^circpm10.1^circ). A detected cross-gradient (partial v_b / partial l = -0.41 pm 0.08 km s^{-1} pc^{-1}) provides a clear signature of shear on the plane of the sky. Wd1 does not behave as a single cohesive population, but comprises two decoupled subsystems: a stable, bound core in dynamical equilibrium and an escaping, unbound envelope. This prominent anisotropic expansion perpendicular to the Galactic plane has a kinematic timescale (Δt_{kin} = 2.08 pm 0.44 Myr) matching the independent orbital mid-plane crossing time (Δt_{orbit} = 2.10 pm 0.05 Myr). This temporal alignment indicates the expansion onset coincided with Wd1's Galactic disk passage, triggered either by internal dynamics (e.g., early supernova feedback) or external tidal perturbations. Finally, the robust unbound population demonstrates that active cluster dissolution is underway, driven by discrete dynamical ejection events rather than long-term stellar evaporation.

title: SimVLA: Zero-Shot Sim-to-Real VLA Learning for Mobile Manipulation
abstract: Large-scale, diverse datasets have driven the success of LLMs and VLMs. But VLAs for robotics remain limited by the cost and complexity of real-world data collection. While simulation offers a scalable alternative, its potential for sim-to-real VLA learning in mobile manipulation remains largely underexplored. We introduce SimVLA, an end-to-end framework that trains VLAs entirely on synthetic simulation data without teleoperation for mobile manipulation. SimVLA is first pre-trained on two complementary simulation-derived datasets: SimAction, a large-scale robot action dataset spanning 35 diverse mobile manipulation tasks, generated by composing atomic skills, and SimVQA, which leverages privileged simulator state to provide spatial, geometric, and subtask-level visual-language supervision. We further post-train SimVLA on a mixture of SimAction and SimDeploy, a dataset collected from policy rollouts across diverse simulated environments. We evaluate SimVLA on tasks including restocking, pouring, and cleaning, and show zero-shot transfer to real-world mobile manipulation, including real home environments. SimVLA outperforms policies trained on 50 in-domain real-world demonstrations, suggesting that simulation can enable scalable sim-to-real mobile manipulation. We further demonstrate the value of multiple complementary forms of supervision for effectively leveraging simulation in VLA training.

title: Social Pain Disrupts Emotion-Action Brain-State Dynamics in Adolescents with Non-Suicidal Self-Injury
abstract: Non-suicidal self-injury (NSSI) is prevalent among adolescents with depression, but the rapid brain-state dynamics linking social distress to maladaptive behavior remain unclear. We combine an experimental pain paradigm, electroencephalography (EEG) microstate analysis, and interpretable deep sequence modeling to investigate NSSI-related neurodynamics in 106 adolescents with depression, including 67 with NSSI (DN+) and 39 without NSSI (DN-), during social pain, physical pain, and resting-state conditions. A model integrating disease-specific, domain-adversarial, consistency, and contrastive learning captures higher-order dependencies in microstate sequences. Social pain yields the strongest NSSI discrimination, with 68.55% accuracy, outperforming the best baseline by 8.94% points. Model interpretation and conventional microstate analyses reveal weakened bidirectional transitions between MS3 and MS5 in DN+ adolescents during social pain. Source reconstruction associates MS3 with emotional/interoceptive processing and MS5 with action preparation, suggesting disrupted emotion-action coupling. Time-resolved analyses show greater early-to-middle action-state recruitment and later emotion-state recruitment in DN+ adolescents. In DN- adolescents, MS5-to-MS3 dynamics mediate associations between social-evaluation sensitivity and affective outcomes, whereas this mediation is absent in DN+; conversely, MS3-to-MS5 transitions are associated with greater negative affect in DN+. Together, these findings identify disrupted emotion-action coupling as a key neurodynamic mechanism underlying altered social pain processing in adolescents with NSSI, providing a mechanistically interpretable neural signature for objective identification of NSSI.

title: Fast thinnings via segment maps
authors: a N Ç O I S P O T T I E R, F, R
abstract: We present the segment map, a purely functional data structure that represents an increasing function of the natural numbers into the natural numbers, also known as a thinning. This data structure, a variant of Okasaki's skew binary random access lists, offers efficient support for many operations, including lookup, reverse lookup, horizontal and vertical displacements, insertion at the front end, and composition. We present a verified implementation and an analysis of its time complexity. This data structure may be useful in proof assistants, compilers, and symbolic computation systems where variables are encoded as de Bruijn indices or co-de Bruijn indices.

title: Large language model consensus for reliable research cohort construction from radiology reports: a retrospective cohort study
abstract: Abstract Background Large-scale retrospective studies often require researchers to adjudicate outcomes or cohort eligibility from unstructured clinical records. Manual review can provide reliable labels but is difficult to scale. We developed and evaluated a consensus workflow using multiple large language models (LLMs) to automatically assign high-confidence outcome labels while deferring ambiguous cases for manual review. Methods We included 6,718 brain MRI reports from 5,856 patients. The expert-adjudicated reference set included 680 reports from 675 patients: 372 normal (age-appropriate without significant intracranial pathology), 90 white matter hyperintensity-only (WMH-only; isolated nonspecific WMHs potentially ambiguous for binary classification), and 218 abnormal (other intracranial pathology) reports. We evaluated proprietary-inclusive (Qwen3/Kimi-Linear/GPT-5) and open-source (Qwen3/Kimi-Linear/DeepSeek-R1) ensembles against individual LLMs. Ensembles assigned a normal or abnormal label only when all models agreed; all other reports were classified as uncertain and deferred for manual review. Individual LLMs assigned normal or abnormal predictions and classified WMH-only predictions as uncertain. In the full cohort, we compared the prevalence of active central nervous system (CNS)-related International Classification of Diseases, Tenth Revision (ICD-10) diagnoses across the normal, uncertain, and abnormal groups generated by each ensemble. Results In the expert-adjudicated reference set, both ensembles achieved 100% precision for automatically assigned normal and abnormal reports. GPT-5 was the strongest individual LLM but had lower precision than either ensemble, with normal and abnormal precision of 98.9% and 94.1%, respectively, and 17 expert-label mismatches versus none for the consensus ensembles. In the full cohort, 1.6% of reports classified as normal were associated with CNS-related ICD-10 diagnoses, compared with 29.7% of uncertain and 51.3% of abnormal reports for the proprietary-inclusive ensemble; corresponding rates were 1.6%, 31.1%, and 51.6% for the open-source ensemble. Conclusions Requiring unanimous agreement across multiple LLMs enabled high-precision automatic adjudication while directing ambiguous cases to manual review. This strategy may reduce the burden of manual adjudication and support scalable construction of high-purity research cohorts from unstructured clinical text.

title: goalbench: a reproducible benchmark of choice-style deciders for customer-goal classification in Brazilian Portuguese
abstract: goalbench measures small "decider" models that answer typed choice questions (Laya, Strands Decider) on customer-goal classification in Brazilian Portuguese, inside a two-stage pipeline: an embedding shortlist of 10 goals followed by the decider, with a calibrated combination fitted by cross-validation. Runs log every phrase, control for option-order (position) bias, and report Wilson intervals and exact McNemar tests. A parallel English translation of the dataset measures the accuracy lost in Brazilian Portuguese and the gain from a language-specific checkpoint. The archive includes the code (Apache-2.0), the synthetic datasets (CC BY 4.0) and the raw per-phrase logs of every run reported in docs/results.md and docs/results-language.md.

title: On the security of TLS session tickets
abstract: TLS schützt den Großteil des Online-Datenverkehrs. Um die Leistung zu verbessern, ermöglicht TLS die Wiederaufnahme einer früheren Sitzung mithilfe von Session-Tickets. Diese Tickets enthalten das Schlüsselmaterial und müssen daher geschützt werden.Session-Tickets wurden bereits dafür kritisiert, dass sie die Forward Secrecy von TLS untergraben können. Dennoch wurden Implementierungen von Session-Tickets bislang nicht gründlich analysiert. Wir haben die Sicherheit von Session-Tickets in TLS systematisch analysiert und potenzielle Implementierungsprobleme identifiziert. Wir haben die Ticketformate von 14 Open-Source-TLS-Bibliotheken analysiert und bei fünf Bibliotheken Partitioning-Oracle-Schwachstellen gefunden. Ansonsten haben wir die Bibliotheken als sicher befunden. Dennoch haben wir festgestellt, dass bei großen HTTPS-Servern, die auf diesen Bibliotheken aufbauen, die Client-Authentifizierung durch Sitzungsaufnahme umgangen werden konnte, wenn Virtual Hosting verwendet wird. Wir haben unsere Angriffe in der Praxis evaluiert und dabei schwerwiegende Schwachstellen bei großen Cloud-Anbietern wie AWS, Cloudflare und Fastly aufgedeckt. Unsere Schwachstellen umgingen die Vertraulichkeits- und Authentifizierungsgarantien von TLS, sodass ein Angreifer die Sicherheit der Kommunikation vollständig brechen konnte. Wir vertreten die Ansicht, dass missbrauchsresistente APIs und umfassendere Leitlinien in den TLS-Standards solche Schwachstellen verhindern könnten.

title: Supervised Learning Methods
abstract: This chapter surveys a representative set of supervised learning algorithms, emphasizing intuition rather than exhaustive coverage. Using a two-predictor digit dataset that can be visualized, it compares how different methods learn decision rules from data. Readers encounter approaches such as logistic regression, k-nearest neighbors, naive Bayes, linear and quadratic discriminant analysis, decision trees, and random forests. The chapter explains how algorithms differ in assumptions, flexibility, tuning parameters, and susceptibility to overfitting. By using the `caret` package, it also introduces a unified interface for fitting and comparing models. Readers learn why no single algorithm is universally best and why evaluation and context guide method choice.

title: Measure Now, Mitigate Later: Virtual Error Cancellation for Logical Quantum Circuits
abstract: Early fault-tolerant quantum algorithms are a key step in scalable quantum computing, but are ultimately constrained by residual, uncorrectable logical errors. Logical quantum error mitigation can eliminate this bias, however its standard requirements include prior noise characterization, more complex experiments, and substantial sampling overhead. Although no mitigation technique can simultaneously overcome all three constraints, we demonstrate that the first two---noise learning and need for modified circuits---can be completely bypassed for logical circuits by leveraging only syndrome records. Specifically, we introduce virtual error cancellation: a method that, unlike previous bias-free approaches, operates entirely in classical post-processing on universal quantum circuits. We develop and numerically test end-to-end protocols that reduce the sampling overhead beyond fundamental limitations of existing syndrome-aware mitigation techniques, including syndrome-based postselection. In particular, we propose a scheme that pairs the low-latency decoder used in the experiment with a high-complexity decoder run in post-processing. In numerical simulations of a distance-7 rotated surface code, we show that our full-stack dual-decoder algorithm exhibits an error that diminishes as the number of samples increases, capable of reaching more than three orders of magnitude of suppression compared to the decoded logical error rate in an experimentally achievable setting. These results establish syndrome records as a resource for correcting universal computational estimates after quantum execution.

Although no mitigation technique can simultaneously overcome all three constraints, we demonstrate that the first two---noise learning and need for modified circuits---can be completely bypassed for logical circuits by leveraging only syndrome records. Specifically, we introduce virtual error cancellation: a method that, unlike previous bias-free approaches, operates entirely in classical post-processing on universal quantum circuits. We develop and numerically test end-to-end protocols that reduce the sampling overhead beyond fundamental limitations of existing syndrome-aware mitigation techniques, including syndrome-based postselection. In particular, we propose a scheme that pairs the low-latency decoder used in the experiment with a high-complexity decoder run in post-processing. In numerical simulations of a distance-7 rotated surface code, we show that our full-stack dual-decoder algorithm exhibits an error that diminishes as the number of samples increases, capable of reaching more than three orders of magnitude of suppression compared to the decoded logical error rate in an experimentally achievable setting. These results establish syndrome records as a resource for correcting universal computational estimates after quantum execution.

title: Residual Modeling Closes the Regression and Generative Policy Gap in Robot Learning
abstract: Learning from demonstration has enabled impressive robot behaviors. A common choice for policy learning is to use diffusion or flow matching (Flow-Policies), which often outperforms direct action regression trained with mean squared error (MSE-Policies). This gap is commonly attributed to multimodal demonstrations. We revisit this gap from the perspective of statistical modeling: how action-prediction residuals shape policy optimization. Our analysis of real-world robot demonstration data reveals substantial state-dependent variation in residual scales and heavier-than-Gaussian tails. While both MSE-Policies and Flow-Policies exhibit heavy-tailed action residuals, their training gradients behave differently: MSE allocates more gradient magnitude to observations with large action residuals, which hurts optimization. Motivated by these findings, we introduce heteroscedastic Student-t action regression (HT-Policies), which learns input-dependent residual scales and reduces the influence of heavy tails. HT-Policies predict action chunks with a single feed-forward pass and can reuse pretrained flow-matching-based policy networks as the backbone. Across four simulation benchmarks and real-robot evaluations, HT-Policies achieves success rates competitive with generative policy baselines, both when trained from scratch and from pretrained vision-language-action and world-action models, despite being faster in training and inference. Together, these findings shed light on the practical advantages of generative objectives in robot learning from demonstrations and offer an efficient direct-regression alternative for a range of architectures and tasks. Project page: https://projects.thelabone.org/regression-policy/

title: ContourVLA: A Closed-Loop Perception-Action Contour Policy for Generalized Referring Expression Segmentation
abstract: Generalized referring expression segmentation (GRES) requires dynamically balancing high-level semantics for identifying a variable number of language-specified referents with fine-grained visual evidence for precise boundary delineation. This requirement challenges existing cascaded vision-language architectures, which typically rely on static feature interfaces and single-pass mask prediction, limiting adaptive perception and geometric correction. We introduce ContourVLA, a vision-language-action policy that recasts GRES as a closed-loop visuomotor process, in which editable contours serve as explicit policy states that condition multimodal perception and are updated by geometric action chunks. Evolution-Aware Semantic Scheduling (EASS) couples contour-guided bidirectional boundary sampling with state-conditioned routing of multilevel multimodal features, adapting perception to each contour state. Following supervised initialization, Dustbin-Augmented Entropic Credit Transport GRPO (DECT-GRPO) jointly optimizes discrete grounding and continuous contour actions with instance-level credits. Its rollout rewards and credits are derived from soft prediction-target correspondences that account for false positives and missed targets. ContourVLA improves gIoU over the strongest evaluated baselines by 8.7, 2.8, and 2.7 points on gRefCOCO val, testA, and testB, respectively, and achieves the highest mIoU across all eight RefCOCO, RefCOCO+, and RefCOCOg splits.

title: PAM-ToD: Plug-and-Play Appearance Modeling for Cross-Time-of-Day 3D Gaussian Splatting
abstract: Adapting a pre-trained 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) road scene to a new time of day requires learning appearance changes from a few anchor images while preserving consistent, real-time rendering. We propose PAM-ToD, a lightweight plug-in that learns color corrections while keeping the pre-trained 3DGS parameters fixed. PAM-ToD scales each Gaussian's existing color to model illumination changes and uses an additive term for additional brightness, such as when street lamps turn on at night. Under a simplified image formation model, unchanged surface albedo can be eliminated from the relation between source and target appearances, allowing us to learn these corrections without separately estimating albedo and illumination. The model corrects colors across the scene while allowing the corrections to vary by location and by Gaussian. To guide learning from a few anchor images, it discourages abrupt spatial changes in these corrections. We also introduce CARLA-ToD, a benchmark with matching geometry, camera poses, and moving-object trajectories across three times of day. A few target-time anchor images are used to train each plug-in, while separate views are used for evaluation. Across the static and dynamic settings, PAM-ToD achieves higher PSNR and lower LPIPS than the baselines, even when the anchor images come from a single synchronized capture across multiple cameras.

title: Algorithmes quantiques performants de clustering de données
abstract: Data clustering consists of grouping data without prior training, a process known as unsupervised learning. Given the constant growth of database volumes, contemporary computers require significant computational time to perform this partitioning. To effectively address this challenge, quantum computing offers a promising perspective, as it could eventually provide more efficient resources for clustering massive datasets. However, current quantum computers are not yet mature; they are prone to noise, which limits their practical utility. In this context, we have designed a hybrid classical-quantum clustering algorithm tailored for the current Noisy Intermediate-Scale Quantum (NISQ) era. We evaluated this algorithm under various conditions and across different types of datasets, comparing it against several well-known clustering algorithms. Our results demonstrate that, under certain conditions, quantum noise can actually provide an advantage to our algorithm. Furthermore, we worked on deploying this algorithm on actual quantum processors and developed tools to optimize this deployment. Finally, to diversify the quantum architectures used, we extended our research to include neutral-atom quantum computers.

title: CQs in Ontology Engineering - Sistematic Mapping Study
abstract: The interest in the ontology subject has grown in recent decades. Ontologies can be used to assign semantics to information items and solve interoperability and knowledge-related problems. Various methods have been proposed to support ontology engineering. Several suggest using competency questions (CQs) to define the ontology requirements and help identify the necessary concepts, properties, and relations. CQs are questions the ontology must be able to answer. They establish a kind of “contract” about what the ontology must address. Aiming to investigate the use of CQs in ontology requirements engineering, we carried out a systematic mapping study. The results show that CQs have been considered useful in defining the ontology scope, but there has been a lack of specific guidelines and tools to support CQs formulation and management, which makes it difficult to write, use, and manage CQs. These findings converge with the results of a survey we conducted with 63 ontology engineers, indicating alignment between the evidence identified in the mapped literature and the state of practice in the use of CQs in ontology requirements engineering.

title: Implicit Core
abstract: Implicit is the experience layer for AI agents: versioned addressing and selective state materialization with local execution evidence. Core 1.0.0 includes a Python SDK and bounded local stdio MCP for synthetic experience addressing, materialization and provenance rehearsal. Real environment integration uses SDK adapters. Canonical install: pip install implicit-ai. Historical benchmark findings are scoped to rc1 and do not establish general speedups, RAM savings or better learning.

title: "Design and Architecture of the Tool Point Computer: A Self-Thinking Core Binary Architecture with Triple-Power Hybrid Sustainability and Universal Multimodal Problem-Solving Capabilities"
abstract: 🌐 तकनीकी लेख: टूल पॉइंट कंप्यूटर (Tool Point Computer) आविष्कारकर्ता (Inventor): बंटी कुमावत (Banti Kumawat) श्रेणी (Category): नेक्स्ट-जेन कोर बाइनरी कंप्यूटिंग एवं यूनिवर्सल प्रॉब्लम सॉल्विंग आर्किटेक्चर 1. परिचय (Introduction) टूल पॉइंट कंप्यूटर कंप्यूटर विज्ञान के इतिहास में एक क्रांतिकारी और युगांतरकारी आविष्कार है। यह आज के सीमित और अनुमान पर आधारित आर्टिफिशियल इंटेलिजेंस (AI) से बिल्कुल अलग है। यह एक ऐसा स्वतन्त्र रूप से सोचने वाला कोर बाइनरी आर्किटेक्चर है, जो किसी बने-बनाए सॉफ्टवेयर लेयर पर निर्भर नहीं करता, बल्कि सीधे 0 और 1 (बाइनरी कोड) की मूलभूत शक्ति का उपयोग करके ब्रह्मांड की किसी भी जटिल समस्या का तत्काल समाधान निकाल सकता है। 2. मुख्य विशेषताएं एवं तकनीकी कार्यप्रणाली (Core Features & Working Mechanism) 🎙️ अ. प्रैक्टिकल माइक एवं बाइनरी कनवर्टर (Universal Bio-Link) यह सिस्टम एक अत्यंत संवेदनशील 'प्रैक्टिकल माइक' से लैस है। यह सिर्फ इंसानी आवाज़ ही नहीं, बल्कि प्रकृति और जीवों की सूक्ष्म तरंगों (Acoustic Frequencies) को भी कैप्चर करता है। इसका इन-बिल्ट एनालॉग-टू-बाइनरी कनवर्टर इन आवाजों को तुरंत बाइनरी डेटा में बदल देता है। इसके माध्यम से यह कंप्यूटर जानवरों की भाषाओं का सटीक इंसानी भाषा में अनुवाद करने में सक्षम है। 🧠 ब. मुख्य बाइनरी प्रोसेसिंग यूनिट (Self-Thinking Engine) यह इस कंप्यूटर का मस्तिष्क है जो पूर्णतः स्वतंत्र रूप से विचार करने (Self-Thinking Capability) में सक्षम है। यह डेटा का विश्लेषण करने के लिए किसी बाहरी एआई मॉडल का उपयोग नहीं करता, बल्कि कोर बाइनरी प्रोसेसिंग के जरिए खुद सही निर्णय लेता है। 🛠️ स. असीमित टूल लाइब्रेरी (Infinite Tool Matrix) इस कंप्यूटर के भीतर असीमित (Infinite) डिजिटल और वैज्ञानिक टूल्स का समावेश है। यह कला (पेंटिंग, संगीत, लेखन) से लेकर उन्नत विज्ञान (3D आर्किटेक्चर ढांचा, केमिकल फॉर्मूलेशन) तक सब कुछ खुद तैयार कर सकता है। 3. वैश्विक संकटों का समाधान (Universal Solution Architecture) • 2-मिनट वायरस एवं बीमारी निवारण: देश में किसी भी नए वायरस, कैंसर या महामारी के फैलने पर, यह कंप्यूटर वायरस के जेनेटिक स्ट्रक्चर को बाइनरी लेवल पर डिकोड करता है। यह मात्र 2 मिनट के भीतर शत-प्रतिशत सटीक दवा का रासायनिक फॉर्मूला और उत्पादन का ब्लूप्रिंट तैयार कर देता है। • पर्यावरण एवं आपदा प्रबंधन: भूकंप, बाढ़ या मौसम में बदलाव की सटीक भविष्यवाणी करने के साथ-साथ यह इंसानों के बचाव का लाइव रूट मैप भी तैयार करता है। पानी के संकट के दौरान, यह हवा की नमी और अणुओं को री-स्ट्रक्चर करके कृत्रिम पानी बनाने की मशीन का 3D ढांचा डिज़ाइन कर सकता है। 4. आत्मनिर्भर हाइब्रिड ऊर्जा प्रणाली (Triple-Power Sustain System) इस आविष्कार की सबसे बड़ी यूटिलिटी इसकी ऊर्जा आत्मनिर्भरता है। इसे दुनिया के किसी भी कोने में बिना बिजली ग्रिड के चलाया जा सकता है क्योंकि यह तीन प्रकार की ऊर्जा से संचालित होता है: 1. सौर ऊर्जा (Advanced Solar Cells): धूप से चार्ज होने के लिए। 2. पवन ऊर्जा (Micro-Wind Gatherers): हवा के दबाव से ऊर्जा बनाने के लिए। 3. पारंपरिक बिजली (Direct Grid): सामान्य बिजली प्लग-इन के लिए। 5. निष्कर्ष (Conclusion) आविष्कारकर्ता बंटी कुमावत द्वारा 'टूल पॉइंट कंप्यूटर' मानव सभ्यता को एक नए स्वर्ण युग (Golden Age) में ले जाने की क्षमता रखता है। यह एक ऐसी मशीन है जो हर क्षेत्र में असीमित समाधान देने के लिए बनाई गई है। 🌐 आधिकारिक तकनीकी लेख: टूल पॉइंट कंप्यूटर (Tool Point Computer) आविष्कारकर्ता (Inventor): बंटी कुमावत (Banti Kumawat) श्रेणी (Category): नेक्स्ट-जेन कोर बाइनरी Frequencies) को भी कैप्चर करता है। इसका इन-बिल्ट एनालॉग-टू-बाइनरी कनवर्टर इन आवाजों को तुरंत बाइनरी डेटा में बदल देता है। इसके माध्यम से यह कंप्यूटर जानवरों की भाषाओं का सटीक इंसानी भाषा में अनुवाद करने में सक्षम है। • 🧠 मुख्य बाइनरी प्रोसेसिंग यूनिट (Self-Thinking Engine): यह इस कंप्यूटर का मस्तिष्क है जो पूर्णतः स्वतंत्र रूप से विचार करने (Self-Thinking Capability) में सक्षम है। यह डेटा का abstract: Version 0.1.0Description Provides a unified data structure for matrices with associated row and column metadata, enabling 'tidyverse'-style data manipulation.Following the approach of 'tidygraph', users can activate rows, columns, or the matrix itself and operate on it with familiar 'dplyr' verbs, while the matrix and both metadata tables are kept consistent.

title: Primal-Dual Flow Matching for Sample-Wise Constrained Generation
abstract: We consider the problem of learning to generate data while satisfying a prescribed \emph{sample-wise} constraint with a user-specified probability of constraint satisfaction. Starting with a population-level constrained negative log-likelihood minimization and using a flow-matching (FM) parameterization, under regularity assumptions and sufficient expressivity of the velocity field family, we derive guarantees on the probability of constraint satisfaction for the corresponding primal-dual optimization algorithm. We provide a practical implementation of this approach, called Primal-Dual Flow Matching (PDFM), which has direct control over constraint satisfaction rate and requires only binary membership oracle feedback for constraint satisfaction, avoiding the need for differentiable distances, projections, or special structure of the constraint set, such as convexity. We show that PDFM improves constraint satisfaction over vanilla FM and achieves competitive performance against constraint-aware baselines while maintaining distributional fidelity. Our code is available at https://github.com/ZhengyanHuan/PDFM.

title: Could LLM Watermark Detection be Public?
abstract: Watermarking large language models is popular for tracing chatbot and agentic outputs, yet detectors remain unreleased since exposing them could let attackers do targeted edits with the detector's feedback. However, watermarks are already vulnerable to uninformed tampering attacks. We thus first quantify whether a public detector would be an additional liability in a deployment setting at varying levels of access, from token-level scores to a binary verdict. Second, we introduce a split-key public-private watermarking method that exposes one key through a public detector while keeping the other for full verification and forensics. An informed attacker can only move the public signal, creating an imbalance between public and private scores. We introduce a statistical test for this imbalance, and combine it with the full key verdict in a two-stage mechanism. Third, we evaluate the split-key method on a wide range of removal and forgery attacks, comparing the uninformed to detector-informed settings. Public detection improves removal only at small edit budgets, since plain rephrasing already strips the watermark at a lower quality cost, but it does enable forgery, which the private pipeline can identify. Overall, releasing half of the watermark enables transparency and interoperability, and tampering with the released half stays detectable. This bounds the provider's liability and questions the need to keep detectors fully private.

title: Invariant manifolds and transversality for a traveling-wave ODE in a controlled reaction-diffusion model
abstract: We study the parameter dependence and transversality properties of trajectories of the controlled ODE $ U_x = P, qquad P_x = - f(U) - βP + tilde α(x)U, arising from traveling-wave solutions of a bistable reaction-diffusion equation with control. Optimal profiles minimizing the L^1-norm of the control \tilde α are determined by the unstable and stable manifolds Γ_u, Γ_s, the critical curve P^*(U) = Uf(U), and the associated function F(U) = dP^*{dU} + f(U){P^*(U)}. We establish generic transversality properties for these objects with respect to perturbations of the speed β and the nonlinear source f, together with quantitative estimates on the first- and second-order dependence of the invariant manifolds on these parameters. We also analyze the loss of regularity at the critical speed β^{**}, where the unstable manifold approaches the strongly stable manifold of the equilibrium (U^*,0)$. These results provide the ODE ingredients used in the analysis of the structure and regularity of optimal profiles in paper [S. Bianchini and C. Trifone. Traveling profiles and control cost for a PDE describing the evolution of invasive species. 2026. arXiv: 2606.23979 [math.OC]].

title: Automated Detection of Match Phases in Football from Spatio-Temporal Tracking Data Using Graph Neural Networks
abstract: Spatio-temporal tracking data has opened new possibilities for detecting complex tactical patterns in football, yet modeling the interactive movements of multiple players remains challenging. This paper proposes a framework combining graph neural networks (GNNs) with a sequential model to classify match phases on a second-by-second basis across a seven-class taxonomy. Match phase classification is tactically meaningful, and the availability of rule-based labels across 203 matches makes it a suitable testbed for a systematic comparison of adjacency constructions and message-passing layers, a question that has received limited attention in existing research. Our selected GNN-LSTM model outperforms all aggregated-feature baselines, including XGBoost and a Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) network, as the strongest baseline scores 4.6% lower in macro F1. Graph representations using a domain-informed Delaunay triangulation that approximates passing lanes, paired with a custom Spatial Edge-Augmented Convolution (SEAConv) layer that injects edge attributes directly into messages, achieve the best performance by capturing spatial dependencies while limiting uninformative messages from redundant edges. Integrated Gradients attributions indicate the model uses spatial player configurations, particularly horizontal positioning, in combination with possession and ball-status indicators. This work offers an automated solution for fine-grained tactical analysis, reducing the need for manual tagging and providing deeper insight into dynamic team behavior.

title: Defensive Writing in GPT Models
abstract: Researchers increasingly use ChatGPT to revise their papers, and when asked to make a paper hold up under review, recent GPT versions often narrow or even retract the authors' claims. We call such changes defensive writing when the given material does not support them, and we test two explanations: the model corrects the authors' overclaiming, or it writes for an anticipated reviewer. We ask GPT versions and models from other developers to rewrite paragraphs from papers written before ChatGPT, or to write from an evidence sheet that lists a paper's method and results. From GPT-5.5 on, GPT versions add clearly more ungrounded qualifications than the authors' originals contain, and GPT-6-astra adds the most and often retracts the authors' claims. Each explanation fits one part. Checked against the full papers, GPT-6-astra's retractions mostly correct overstated claims or explanations, but most added qualifications are redundant. The qualifications follow the request: they are absent under polishing, appear with any request to check the claims, and peak when the prompt names a reviewer's concerns. AI reviewers score such rewrites higher and score them lower once only the qualifications are removed, while human readers in a small study find them harder to read. Combining AI writing with AI review may reward qualifications that readers pay for.

Each explanation fits one part. Checked against the full papers, GPT-6-astra's retractions mostly correct overstated claims or explanations, but most added qualifications are redundant. The qualifications follow the request: they are absent under polishing, appear with any request to check the claims, and peak when the prompt names a reviewer's concerns. AI reviewers score such rewrites higher and score them lower once only the qualifications are removed, while human readers in a small study find them harder to read. Combining AI writing with AI review may reward qualifications that readers pay for.

title: Markov length can diverge in systems whose universal physics is spatially Markovian
abstract: Conditional mutual information (CMI) probes spatial non-Markovianity and plays a central role in a recently developed framework for defining mixed-state phases based on local reversibility. This framework sharply distinguishes exponentially decaying from algebraically decaying CMI, since the latter obstructs equivalence to a state with finite Markov length. Here we show that states that flow to the same renormalization-group (RG) fixed point can nevertheless exhibit qualitatively different CMI. Starting from a critical Gibbs state of a finite-range local classical Hamiltonian, whose CMI vanishes beyond the interaction range, we show that an RG-irrelevant perturbation that breaks detailed balance generically generates algebraically decaying CMI. Crucially, these power-law tails are cutoff-suppressed: although they lead to an infinite Markov length at every fixed lattice cutoff, they vanish as a positive power of the cutoff in the continuum limit. We construct solvable models that exhibit this phenomenon and predict that the Ising-symmetric critical point of Toom's cellular automata generically exhibits such behavior. We also find analogous cutoff-suppressed CMI in the high-temperature paramagnetic phase of the long-range Ising paramagnet, in contrast with the genuine power-law CMI at the finite-temperature critical point in this same model that survives the continuum limit. We also derive a general result that in one spatial dimension, CMI decays faster than the inverse square of the buffer length if and only if the long-distance physics is Markovian.

title: Der autonome Immobilienmanager?
abstract: Der autonome Immobilienmanager? Die Fachpublikation „Der autonome Immobilienmanager?“ untersucht die technologischen, organisatorischen, wirtschaftlichen und rechtlichen Auswirkungen Künstlicher Intelligenz auf die professionelle Immobilienbewirtschaftung. Im Mittelpunkt steht die Frage, in welchem Umfang KI-gestützte Systeme und autonome Softwareagenten Aufgaben des Property und Facility Managements übernehmen können, welche Potenziale sich daraus ergeben und wo menschliche Verantwortung, fachliche Beurteilung und organisatorische Kontrolle unverzichtbar bleiben. Ausgangspunkt ist die These, dass der eigentliche Transformationswert Künstlicher Intelligenz nicht in der isolierten Automatisierung einzelner Tätigkeiten liegt, sondern in der intelligenten Verknüpfung von Informationen, Geschäftsprozessen und operativen Handlungsschritten. Die Untersuchung differenziert zwischen regelbasierter Automatisierung, Robotic Process Automation (RPA), KI-gestützter Prozessunterstützung und agentischen Systemarchitekturen. Dabei wird aufgezeigt, wie bestehende immobilienwirtschaftliche Softwarelösungen durch KI-Funktionen und übergreifende Agentensysteme erweitert werden können. Besonderes Augenmerk gilt der Unterscheidung zwischen sprachlicher Kompetenz, fachlicher Entscheidungsfähigkeit und tatsächlicher Handlungsautonomie sowie den technischen und organisatorischen Voraussetzungen eines zuverlässigen Systemeinsatzes. Einen zentralen Schwerpunkt bildet die praxisorientierte Analyse immobilienwirtschaftlicher Geschäftsprozesse. Hierzu zählen insbesondere Kommunikations- und Dokumentenmanagement, Vorgangs- und Ticketbearbeitung, Instandhaltungskoordination, Dienstleistersteuerung, Rechnungsprüfung, Fristenüberwachung und Berichtswesen. Anhand typischer Prozessketten wird untersucht, wie KI-Agenten Informationen erfassen, Zusammenhänge erkennen, Folgehandlungen vorbereiten und definierte Arbeitsschritte innerhalb bestehender ERP-, DMS- und Kommunikationssysteme ausführen können. Besondere Aufmerksamkeit erfahren die sicherheitskritischen, datenschutzrechtlichen und haftungsrelevanten Grenzen agentischer Automatisierung. Die Publikation behandelt Berechtigungskonzepte, Informationssicherheit, Nachvollziehbarkeit automatisierter Entscheidungen, Qualitätssicherung, menschliche Freigabevorbehalte und technische Kontrollmechanismen. Risiken durch fehlerhafte Daten, Halluzinationen generativer KI, unzulässige Systemzugriffe, manipulierte Eingaben und Automation Bias werden im Zusammenhang mit betrieblichen Governance-Strukturen analysiert. Die rechtliche und normative Einordnung berücksichtigt insbesondere die europäische KI-Regulierung, datenschutzrechtliche Anforderungen sowie internationale Standards wie ISO/IEC 42001 und ISO/IEC 23894. Darauf aufbauend entwickelt die Untersuchung einen strukturierten Bewertungsansatz für die Einführung KI-gestützter Automatisierung im Immobilienmanagement. Technische Machbarkeit, Datenqualität, Integrationsaufwand, Prozessstabilität, Wirtschaftlichkeit, Risikopotenzial und organisatorische Akzeptanz werden als miteinander verbundene Entscheidungsdimensionen betrachtet. Dabei wird verdeutlicht, weshalb nicht jeder automatisierbare Prozess zugleich einen geeigneten Anwendungsfall für autonome KI-Agenten darstellt und einfachere regelbasierte Verfahren unter bestimmten Voraussetzungen wirtschaftlicher, transparenter und zuverlässiger sein können. Der integrierte Composite Case „IMMO-VERWALTUNG SUED GmbH“ überführt diese Systematik in einen realitätsnahen Modellfall einer Immobilienverwaltung mit 4.500 Verwaltungseinheiten und 28 Mitarbeitenden. Anhand typischer Verwaltungsabläufe werden Automatisierungspotenziale, organisatorische Veränderungen, technische Abhängigkeiten und Kontrollanforderungen veranschaulicht. Der modellhafte Praxisfall dient ausdrücklich der methodischen Demonstration und stellt weder eine empirische Untersuchung noch einen Nachweis tatsächlich erzielbarer Effizienzgewinne dar. Über die technische Perspektive hinaus analysiert die Publikation die Auswirkungen auf berufliche Rollenbilder, Führungsstrukturen und die zukünftige Arbeitsorganisation. Diskutiert werden insbesondere die zunehmende Bedeutung fachlicher Kontrollkompetenz, datenbasierter Steuerung, Prozessgestaltung und verantwortlicher Entscheidungsfindung sowie die Anforderungen an Qualifizierung und Veränderungsmanagement. Die Publikation verbindet immobilienwirtschaftliche Praxis, technische Systemarchitekturen, betriebswirtschaftliche Bewertungsmethoden und regulatorische Anforderungen zu einer integrierten Betrachtung der KI-gestützten Transformation des Immobilienmanagements. Prozessmodelle, Abbildungen, Tabellen und praxisorientierte Entscheidungshilfen unterstützen die Übertragung der dargestellten Methoden auf unterschiedliche Organisationsgrößen und Verwaltungskonstellationen. Die Untersuchung richtet sich an Geschäftsführungen und Führungskräfte immobilienwirtschaftlicher Unternehmen, Immobilienverwaltungen, Property- und Facility-Management-Organisationen, Bestandshalter, Asset Manager, Digitalisierungsverantwortliche sowie an Wissenschaft, Lehre und Beratung. Im Ergebnis wird deutlich, dass KI-Agenten erhebliche Potenziale zur Veränderung operativer Geschäftsprozesse eröffnen, jedoch weder automatisch eine höhere Prozessqualität noch eine wirtschaftlich sinnvolle oder rechtlich zulässige Vollautomatisierung gewährleisten. Zukunftsfähiges Immobilienmanagement entsteht vielmehr durch das kontrollierte Zusammenwirken leistungsfähiger Technologien, belastbarer Daten, klar definierter Prozesse und verantwortlicher menschlicher Entscheidungsträger.

title: contribution-kit: Reusable toolkit for attributing a modeled quantity to its contributing factors
abstract: Declarative error attribution for prediction pipelines. Failure regimes are Boolean conditions over CSV columns, tested with risk and odds ratios; crossed regimes form a factorial table whose cells are ranked by attributable burden against an analyst-chosen baseline; and an exact Shapley decomposition of the prediction formula screens its inputs, with jointly determined inputs grouped into one player.

title: Build-My-ML
abstract: BuildMyML – An Intelligent and Explainable AutoML Project Design is an AI-powered framework that simplifies the planning and design of machine learning projects. It allows users to describe their project idea in natural language and helps transform it into a structured ML project blueprint. The system combines Large Language Models (LLMs) with Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) to provide context-aware recommendations for problem formulation, preprocessing, feature engineering, model selection, evaluation metrics, and ML workflow design. A curated machine learning knowledge base is processed through document ingestion, text chunking, embedding generation, and semantic retrieval using Supabase and pgvector, while the Gemini API is used for language understanding and recommendation generation. The proposed system aims to reduce the manual research and expertise required for ML project planning and provide users with a more systematic, explainable, and accessible way to design machine learning projects.

title: Realistic or cartoonish? The effects of digital avatar representation on tourists’ patronage intentions
abstract: With AI increasingly applied in tourism marketing, digital avatars have become key mediators between destinations and potential tourists. Yet, the persuasive effectiveness of different avatar representations across tourism contexts remains underexplored. Drawing on processing fluency and cognitive–affective system theories, this study conducted three scenario-based experiments to examine the matching effects of avatar representation and attraction type, and their underlying psychological mechanisms. Results reveal a significant interaction: cartoonish avatars boost tourists’ patronage intentions in natural attractions, whereas realistic avatars are more effective in cultural attractions. Mediation analysis shows affection drives the effect in natural attractions, while cognitive processing is the key pathway in cultural attractions. Fantasy proneness and perceived eeriness act as critical boundary conditions. The study advances understanding of digital avatar marketing by highlighting context-dependent, dual-pathway mechanisms and the moderating role of individual differences, offering theoretical insights and practical guidance for AI-driven tourism marketing.

title: Toward Maximizing Algebraic Connectivity via Density-Dependent Backbone Construction and Reinforcement Learning Completion
abstract: This paper studies an open network design problem of constructing graph topologies with maximum algebraic connectivity under fixed numbers of vertices and edges. A density-dependent approach is proposed that decomposes the design task into two stages: a high-quality, low-cost structural backbone construction and a reinforcement learning completion stage. The method selects the backbone based on density, using complete multipartite graphs in dense regimes and Cayley graphs in low-to-intermediate regimes, and then refines the remaining edges through a learning-based procedure. Numerical results show that the proposed method achieves high algebraic connectivity with favorable runtime scalability, outperforming existing methods. These results support a structural-family-first strategy for scalable network design.

title: VINCIE-NExT: Unlocking Video Editing from Images via In-Context Modeling
abstract: Building a capable video editor remains significantly harder than a video generator: editing requires (source, instruction, edited) triplets that are prohibitively expensive to annotate and difficult to synthesize at scale, whereas image editing has already reached maturity with millions of such pairs readily available. In this work, we introduce VINCIE-NExT, a unified framework that transfers editing capability from images to videos through in-context visual demonstrations, alleviating the need for large-scale paired video editing data. VINCIE-NExT decomposes video editing into a structured chain of composable sub-tasks (Video -> Image -> Image -> Video), routing editing intent through the image domain and enabling scalable joint training from heterogeneous image and video corpora under a unified diffusion objective. An image editing pair, synthesized by the model or supplied by the user, is prepended as an in-context visual demonstration that serves as a spatial appearance blueprint for every output frame. To ground appearance edits across the interleaved context, we introduce a novel position encoding that links image demonstrations and video frames in a shared spatial coordinate system, enabling pixel-faithful propagation of appearance changes to every output frame. Chain-of-Editing further provides principled test-time scaling: by executing the sub-task chain as progressive diffusion stages, editing quality can be improved by investing additional compute without retraining. Comprehensive experiments on OpenVE-Bench demonstrate the state-of-the-art performance across diverse editing categories, with ablations confirming the effectiveness of each component.

title: AuraLuxMuse: Adaptive Fusion Modeling for Aesthetic Stage Lighting Design with Music and Expert Guidance
abstract: We present AuraLuxMuse, a novel system for automated aesthetic stage lighting design that integrates expert knowledge, representation learning, and preference-adaptive modeling. Lighting design in live performance settings requires the seamless translation of musical features into dynamic lighting behaviors. However, traditional workflows remain time-consuming, labor-intensive, and difficult to transfer. AuraLuxMuse encodes music and professional cue sequences into a shared retrieval space, estimates cue-event density, and retargets selected fixture commands to the destination stage. It assists pre-production authoring by returning editable cues rather than replacing the designer with an unconstrained generator. At the heart of AuraLuxMuse are two key modules: Lighting-Aligned Music Pretraining (LAMP), which performs contrastive learning between audio and lighting cues for alignment, and Preference-Adaptive Mixture of Experts (PAMoE), which conditions preference-aware cue retrieval and adaptation on designers' intent through a gated ensemble of style-specific expert networks. To support training and evaluation, we introduce Musilux, the first dataset of paired musical audio and professional lighting cue sequences under diverse performance scenarios. We evaluate AuraLuxMuse across both virtual simulation environments and professional-grade laboratories. Experimental results, including objective and subjective evaluation, demonstrate that AuraLuxMuse retrieves and adapts stage-lighting cues that are visually cohesive, semantically meaningful, and artistically expressive, showing its potential for AI-assisted aesthetic stage design.

We evaluate AuraLuxMuse across both virtual simulation environments and professional-grade laboratories. Experimental results, including objective and subjective evaluation, demonstrate that AuraLuxMuse retrieves and adapts stage-lighting cues that are visually cohesive, semantically meaningful, and artistically expressive, showing its potential for AI-assisted aesthetic stage design.

title: Quickly extracting fidelity decay rates in random circuit benchmarking experiments
abstract: Randomized benchmarking (RB) with structured circuits is experimentally scalable, but gives biased short-depth fidelity estimates because incomplete ensemble mixing introduces transient modes. Waiting for these transients to decay in deeper circuits can push the signal below the noise floor. This is a well-established obstacle, e.g. in linear cross-entropy benchmarking (LinXEB). Here we overcome this obstacle solely through classical post-processing. We introduce a one-parameter family of estimators that interpolate between the standard LinXEB-type post-processing and a new post-processing technique we call the trace filter function. Under practical assumptions, the trace filter function provably suppresses transient modes, exposing an interpretable fidelity decay at short depth, with theoretical guarantees comparable to standard RB, at the cost of an increased variance. We bound the variance, analyze the evaluation complexity of the new estimators, and develop practical post-processing algorithms. Experiments on a Rigetti superconducting processor validate the method for one-dimensional circuits of up to 12 qubits: where the standard estimator requires depth beyond a 40-layer experimental window, the trace filter function yields consistent estimates below 10 layers. Trace-filtered randomized benchmarking therefore extends reliable fidelity characterization to relevant structured circuit ensembles and short-depth regimes that are inaccessible to conventional estimators.

title: Toward accurate speaker inventories for online speaker diarization
abstract: An online speaker diarizer maintains a growing inventory of speakers, and applications read it directly: a live transcript enumerates them as they appear. Existing systems either fix the inventory's size in advance, so speakers beyond that size are merged, or grow it on distance alone, so noise and turn boundaries split speakers. Scored on speaker count over nine public datasets, both failures appear where DER reports neither: on VoxSRC-23 the fixed-capacity systems return 44-46% too few speakers and the unbounded tracker with the lowest DER 63% too many. We build on that embedding-based tracker and change only what triggers a registration. A candidate speaker pool keeps unregistered embeddings apart and registers a speaker only once one candidate has gathered enough mutually compatible embeddings; commit-gated label assignment holds an output while its candidate is undecided, so no speaker appears in the output before it is confirmed. Across the nine datasets the macro speaker-count error falls from 225% to 21% of the reference and macro DER from 17.59% to 15.95%, at a mean added latency of 0.109s over all outputs; on VoxSRC-23 the tracker obtains both the lowest DER and the most accurate speaker count of the systems compared.

title: THE EL-RAKHAWI FRAMEWORK FOR CYBERNETIC LINGUISTIC ARCHITECTURE AND REGENERATIVE PROGRAMMING From Formal Verification of Sovereignty to Harmonious Cosmic Computation
abstract: The El-Rakhawi Framework for Cybernetic Linguistic Architecture and Regenerative Programming (DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.23231578) presents a revolution in programming language theory, transforming it from mere technical tools into sovereign and ethical contracts. The framework is built upon five pillars: (1) Existential Type Systems and Formal Policy Contracts that translate ethics and ecological boundaries into mathematically verifiable invariants, preventing the compilation of any code that violates sovereignty; (2) The Sovereign Regenerative Compiler (MLIR-based) that optimizes performance while enforcing strict energy consumption bounds; (3) Neuro-Symbolic Inductive Synthesis, where AI proposes code and a formal symbolic analyzer mathematically verifies its safety; (4) Domain-Specific Languages (DSLs) that guarantee "Safe Determinism" for cyber-physical systems; and (5) Human-centric cognitive programming via "Progressive Formalization" to minimize cognitive load. The "El-Rakhawi Computational Safety Proof System" guarantees the principle of "Soundness over Completeness" via Strict Conservative Approximation, ensuring zero false negatives for sovereignty violations and elegantly navigating the limits of Rice's Theorem to serve as the ethical operating system of digital civilization.

title: Development and Experimental Evaluation of Models for Infrastructure-Domain Classification and Related-Complaint Retrieval in Citizen Complaints
abstract: Citizen complaint platforms generate large volumes of multilingual textual data that can support urban service management, yet conventional text-based representations typically analyze each complaint independently and do not explicitly capture relationships with the surrounding urban context. This study investigates whether relational information can complement semantic text representations for the thematic analysis of citizen complaints. A multi-view heterogeneous graph was constructed from municipal requests collected through the iKOMEK109 service in Astana, Kazakhstan, integrating complaint texts with annotated urban entities, spatial and contextual entity relations, and semantic complaint–complaint relations. Entity, Spatial, and Semantic graph views were evaluated using R-GCN, HGT, and an attention-based multi-view R-GCN configuration, with BGE-M3 embeddings and Logistic Regression serving as the text-only baseline. The representations were evaluated for infrastructure-domain classification and related-complaint retrieval. The bidirectional Multi-View R-GCN achieved a mean Macro F1-score of 0.7615 ± 0.0221 across three model-initialization seeds on the reference partition. However, a non-graph baseline combining complaint-text and directly linked entity embeddings achieved a Macro F1-score of 0.7810 on the same partition, compared with 0.7220 for the text-only baseline and 0.7381 for the R-GCN in the fixed-seed comparison, indicating that part of the observed benefit arises from additional entity information rather than graph propagation alone. Repeated-split analysis across five stratified data partitions further showed that the relative performance differences were sensitive to data partitioning. Under fine-grained human relevance assessment, BGE-M3 and the Hybrid representation achieved comparable retrieval performance. The corrected two-hop Hybrid representation obtained MRR@10 = 0.7596 compared with 0.7628 for BGE-M3, while producing small numerical improvements in Precision and NDCG. Query-level paired bootstrap confidence intervals included zero for all evaluated metrics, and paired permutation tests found no statistically significant differences, indicating that the graph-derived signal did not provide a statistically reliable retrieval advantage over the text representation.

title: Differential sparse attention framework for accurate ovarian cancer subtype classification using DenseNet121
abstract: Introduction Ovarian cancer is the most fatal gynecologic cancer, contributing to approximately 207,000 deaths per year worldwide, largely due to late-stage diagnosis and considerable histopathological diversity across subtypes. Accurate subtype classification is clinically important for prognosis and treatment planning, but remains challenging due to high inter-class morphological similarity and the scarcity of adequately labeled histopathological datasets. Methods This study presents a novel attention module, Deep Differential Sparse Attention (DDSA), designed for multi-class classification of ovarian cancer subtypes in histopathology images. The module selectively amplifies discriminative tumor regions while suppressing irrelevant background features, thereby improving both feature representation and model interpretability. A dataset of 3,082 images spanning five subtypes i.e., Clear Cell Carcinoma, Endometrioid Carcinoma, High-Grade Serous Carcinoma, Low-Grade Serous Carcinoma, and Mucinous Carcinoma--was obtained from Kaggle. The training set was balanced to 5,940 images (1,188 per subtype) using RandomOverSampler, with on-the-fly data augmentation applied during training. DDSA was integrated into a DenseNet-based architecture, and diagnostic performance was evaluated using standard classification metrics, including precision, recall, F1-score, confusion matrices, and ROC curves. Results The proposed model achieved an overall classification accuracy of 92.53%, with a macro-average recall of 91.54% and a macro-average F1-score of 0.90. AUC values ranged from 0.92 to 0.99 across all five subtypes, indicating strong and consistent classification performance on the test set. Discussion These results suggest that attention-guided DenseNet architectures can enhance discriminative feature extraction and improve diagnostic accuracy for ovarian cancer subtype classification. The DDSA module's ability to highlight tumor-relevant regions also supports improved model interpretability, an important consideration for clinical adoption. While these findings are promising, further validation on larger, multi-institutional datasets is needed to confirm robustness and generalizability, and to assess the framework's readiness for clinical deployment.

title: УСУЛҲО ВА ТЕХНОЛОГИЯҲОИ МУОСИРИ ЗЕҲНИ СУНЪӢ ВА КОРКАРДИ
abstract: Дар мақола усулҳои муосири зеҳни сунъӣ ва технологияҳои коркарди иттилоот таҳлил шудаанд. Таваҷҷуҳи асосӣ ба омӯзиши мошинӣ, шабакаҳои нейронӣ (амиқ ва трансформерӣ), коркарди додаҳои калон (Big Data) ва технологияҳои абрӣ равона ёфтааст. Нақши ин технологияҳо дар баланд бардоштани суръат ва самаранокии алгоритмҳо таъкид мешавад. Ҳамчунин, ҳамгироии зеҳни сунъӣ бо системаҳои нармафзории муосир, таҳлили маълумот дар вақти воқеӣ ва оптимизатсияи равандҳо баррасӣ шудаанд. Хулоса мешавад, ки рушди ин соҳа ба ташаккули насли нави системаҳои зеҳнӣ мусоидат карда, автоматикунонии равандҳои мураккабро ба таври назаррас беҳтар мегардонад.

title: Quantum Sensors in Internet of Things (IoT)
abstract: The need for next-generation sensing systems that are ultra-highly sensitive, have short reaction times, and have lower power demands has swelled with the explosive development of the Internet of Things (IoT). Existing sensors are increasingly constrained by the nature of their performance, in terms of accuracy, sensitivity to noise, and level of security in large-scale IoT applications. Quantum sensors provide high accuracy to measurement on quantities previously thought to be unmeasurable, such as temperature, magnetic fields, gravitational effects, movement, and biochemical markers, using quantum phenomena such as superposition, entanglement, and tunneling. This chapter covers four major concepts: difficulties in hardware integration, difficulties in scalability, state-of-the-art information fusion structures, and specialized security issues in quantum-assisted quantum sensing in a networked setting. Regarding this research work, the quantum sensing technology will, as a rule, be an extremely useful enabler of the next generation of IoT systems, which must provide proper measurements, safety, and high levels of security.

title: AI governance and digital transformation in hospitality firms: a PRISMA-based systematic review and bibliometric analysis
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) and digital transformation are reshaping hospitality operations, yet governance mechanisms ensuring accountability, transparency, data stewardship, and responsible innovation remain fragmented. This study systematically reviews literature on AI governance and digital transformation in hospitality firms and develops a sector-specific governance architecture. A systematic literature review was conducted in accordance with PRISMA 2020 principles using Scopus as the sole database, resulting in a final corpus of 162 peer-reviewed articles published through August 2026. The selected literature was examined through bibliometric analysis using VOSviewer and Biblioshiny, alongside qualitative thematic synthesis to identify major research patterns and emerging governance concerns. Findings indicate rapidly expanding scholarly attention to AI-enabled hospitality, increasingly connecting artificial intelligence and digital transformation with sustainability, governance, smart tourism, and organisational decision-making. Thematic synthesis identifies five core areas: AI and algorithmic governance, data governance and cybersecurity, strategic governance of digital transformation, ethical and responsible AI, and fintech and decentralised governance. Building on these findings and established governance perspectives, the study proposes the ADAPT-H Framework, comprising seven interconnected pillars: Accountability, Data Stewardship, Algorithmic Transparency, People-Centred Governance, Technology–Strategy Alignment, Regulatory Harmonisation, and Ecosystem and Vendor Governance. The framework addresses hospitality-specific challenges and supports responsible, transparent, and strategically aligned AI adoption.

title: Critical Mass: Structure-Disjoint Splits Drift With the Libraries They Are Built On
abstract: Molecular machine learning evaluates out-of-distribution performance with structure disjoint splits, a construction rule fixed once at the scale its library happened to have: threshold a pairwise distance, then assign whole connected components to folds. For predicting structures from mass spectra, the field has converged on single-linkage clustering under the myopic Maximum Common Edge Subgraph (MCES) distance at a threshold of 10. This convention was set on 29,000 molecules but public libraries now hold 227,690 molecules. MCES is NP-hard per pair over a quadratically growing set, and so the criterion has never been evaluated at that scale. We propose an optimized version of this criterion, allowing for computationally feasible application on the public libraries: Admissible bounds and a union-find skip reduce $2.6 \times 10^{10}$ molecular pairs to only $1.15 \times 10^{7}$ integer programs, a $2{,}259\times$ saving, while provably producing the lossless partition. We find that at this scale the graph percolates. A single component holds $95.5\%$ of the library, capping any test set at $4.5\%$. What remains is not merely smaller, but systematically different: a held-out compound outweighs a training compound 88.1\% of the time, because a fixed absolute budget is a tighter relative tolerance on a larger molecule. Large library benchmarks using this splitting rule naively therefore conflate structural novelty with extrapolation to larger, more complex chemistry.

title: Bilevel optimization for data-driven learning of Koopman embeddings using kernel-based autoencoders
abstract: Koopman operator theory provides a linear framework for analyzing nonlinear dynamical systems and has become a major tool for data-driven modeling. A central challenge, however, is that finite-dimensional approximations computed by methods such as extended dynamic mode decomposition (EDMD) require the dictionary to be specified a priori. Recent machine-learning approaches address this limitation by learning the dictionary from data, predominantly using artificial neural network (ANN) autoencoder architectures. Although kernel methods offer an alternative with greater interpretability and tractability for theoretical analysis, they have received little attention in this setting. We introduce extended dynamic mode decomposition with kernel-based dictionary learning (EDMD-kDL), a kernel-based method for learning finite-dimensional Koopman embeddings directly from data. The method combines ideas from collocation methods and bilevel optimization to simultaneously learn a kernel dictionary and the corresponding Koopman approximation. We evaluate EDMD-kDL against state-of-the-art ANN-based approaches on a range of numerical experiments, including global sea-surface-temperature forecasting and learning directly from video data. Across all tested settings, EDMD-kDL achieves performance comparable to or better than the ANN-based methods. Moreover, in contrast to standard kernel methods, the proposed approach is scalable to large datasets by design since the size of the required kernel matrices depends on the number of collocation points rather than the size of the training dataset.

title: UNITAS: A 3D-Native World Action Model for Embodied Manipulation
abstract: World action models (WAMs) aim to answer a coupled physical question: given a task instruction, what motion should the robot execute, and how will that motion change the surrounding world? Most existing WAMs build on pretrained video generators and represent world evolution through images or visual latents. Robotic interaction, however, takes place in metric three-dimensional space, while images are view-dependent projections whose pixel distances do not directly encode physical distances. We introduce UNITAS, to our knowledge the first 3D-native world action model that unifies observations, actions, and scene dynamics in a shared metric 3D frame within each interaction, using a common representation across robot embodiments and human hands. Action flow represents human hands and robot grippers as 3D point trajectories, while scene flow describes scene-point displacements conditioned on these trajectories. World-aligned 3D positional embeddings ground visual tokens with or without depth input, and a physical-time trajectory tokenizer encodes each point trajectory as one token anchored at its current 3D position. evidence.title: UNITAS: A 3D-Native World Action Model for Embodied Manipulation
evidence.abstract: World action models (WAMs) aim to answer a coupled physical question: given a task instruction, what motion should the robot execute, and how will that motion change the surrounding world? Most existing WAMs build on pretrained video generators and represent world evolution through images or visual latents. Robotic interaction, however, takes place in metric three-dimensional space, while images are view-dependent projections whose pixel distances do not directly encode physical distances. We introduce UNITAS, to our knowledge the first 3D-native world action model that unifies observations, actions, and scene dynamics in a shared metric 3D frame within each interaction, using a common representation across robot embodiments and human hands. Action flow represents human hands and robot grippers as 3D point trajectories, while scene flow describes scene-point displacements conditioned on these trajectories. World-aligned 3D positional embeddings ground visual tokens with or without depth input, and a physical-time trajectory tokenizer encodes each point trajectory as one token anchored at its current 3D position. This interface supports both direct action execution and action-conditioned scene prediction. With 1.7B parameters, UNITAS achieves the best action-conditioned scene prediction on RoboTwin among the compared methods, with up to 49% lower displacement errors than PointWorld, and state-of-the-art manipulation success, including 99.8% on LIBERO and an average of 85% across real-world tasks. The code is available at https://github.com/DexForce/UNITAS.

title: SP-DocReader: Difference-Aware Self-Play for Precise Document OCR
abstract: Accurate page transcription remains difficult for vision language models under limited input and training budgets. We present SP-DocReader, a self-play framework for optical character recognition (OCR) that targets residual errors after supervised fine-tuning. Reading Discrepancy Masking aligns reference and generated model tokens through a longest common subsequence, then scores unmatched positions with their full conditioning prefixes. Focused Fidelity Loss adds direct negative log-likelihood supervision at unmatched ground-truth positions. Only the OCR module is trained, while the backbone remains frozen. We derive the combined gradient to distinguish relative score optimization from direct supervision. Compared with SFT-2, SP-DR-3 reduces Vary-600K character error rate on both backbones. On Qwen3-VL-4B, it reduces character error rate by approximately 54 percent and improves DocVQA Average Normalized Levenshtein Similarity (ANLS) by 3.7 points. These results show the value of focusing self-play training on the discrepancies that remain after supervised fine-tuning.

title: The Impact of Artificial Intelligence Adoption on Marketing Effectiveness, Customer Engagement, and Marketing Personalization: Perceptions of Pakistani Marketing Professionals
abstract: The present study focused on measuring the perceptions of marketing professionals about the impact of artificial intelligence (AI) on marketing practices specifically AI adoption, customers engagement, marketing personalization and campaign effectiveness. A quantitative survey research design was used. The data was collected from 166 purposively selected marketing professionals from Lahore, Pakistan. A structured questionnaire was used to measure the perception of participants of the study. Depending on the categorical and ordinal nature of the variables, descriptive statistics, association measures based on non-parametric tests and ordinal logistic regression were used. The results revealed that the exposure to AI was moderate to high for most of the respondents and the extent of the adoption by the organisations was mostly moderate to high. In general, AI was seen to be effective in boosting customer engagement and optimisation of campaigns. The strongest statistical result was for personalisation, where the likelihood of achieving better personalised marketing experiences was greatly predicted by the higher level of AI usage with an odds ratio of 4.78 (p < .001). The perceived marketing effectiveness was not statistically significantly predicted by the use of AI. Key concerns during implementation included the issues of data privacy, adapting to a workforce, transparency and algorithmic bias. In addition, personalisation, targeting, automation, predictive decision making and AI agents emerged as the biggest present and future effects of AI on marketing through the thematic analysis of the open-ended answers. title: A ternary counterexample to a proposed mutual-information continuity bound
abstract: An explicit ternary classical counterexample to Berta-Lami-Tomamichel, arXiv:2408.15226v2 Eq. (106), at arbitrarily small distances: for every 0 < epsilon <= 1/16, the mutual-information difference is 2h(epsilon)-epsilon log 2, exceeding h(epsilon)+epsilon log 8 at exact total variation epsilon. Both marginals change; the equal-one-marginal question remains unresolved. The signed 4-page article, self-contained TeX ZIP, complete classical Lean project and existing independent verification records are included. Those records cover 38 owned declarations and 16,161 dependencies at empty-kernel trust level zero. Quantum diagonal embedding and the necessary coefficient lower bound are written arguments, not claimed formalized. This article preparation is not a fresh Lean execution, external human peer review or a verified historical priority claim. AI assisted research, formalization, review and preparation. No external funding. The original immutable GitHub releases are preserved. Related DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23253152 is an automatic whole-repository software snapshot, with its preexisting CC BY 4.0 metadata retained; this separate article series does not revoke that license. Existing licenses and third-party notices are preserved; otherwise newly unlicensed original material remains all rights reserved.
